text:
Clipboard copies groups of settlement objects into reusable patterns. Select
objects, save a pattern, then paste it relative to the Clipboard tool's position
and rotation. You can also move, rotate, scale, or scrap a selection.

text:
1. Build the Clipboard Tool from the workshop's Special category.
2. Activate its controls and choose a selection method: All, Box, Sphere,
   Cylinder, By Cell, By Plugin, or the manual selection gun.
3. Select the objects you want, then save them to a pattern slot. Confirming an
   overwrite replaces that slot; cancelling leaves the existing pattern intact.
4. Place the tool at the destination and choose a saved pattern to paste.
   The tool's position and rotation determine where the group appears.
5. Wait for the import to finish before starting another operation. Review any
   warning about objects, wires, or power that could not be prepared.

Pattern files are stored at Data\F4SE\Plugins\Clipboard\<slot>\pattern.ini.
Back up your own pattern files before reinstalling or replacing slot folders.

Rotation accepts degrees greater than 0 and up to 180, with up to six decimal
places. Use a dot as the decimal separator, for example 12.345678. Choose whether
to rotate around the selection's center or the Clipboard tool.

text:
Increase and Decrease take a relative percentage change. Increase accepts more
than 0 and up to 1000; Decrease accepts more than 0 and up to 99. Up to six
decimal places are allowed, but every resulting object size must be an exact
whole-number percentage between 1% and 1000% of its original size. A valid
number may still be unsuitable for the selected sizes. Clipboard rejects it
before changing objects and shows valid increments, limits or nearby values.

text:
For example, increasing 100% objects by 12% makes them 112%. Increasing a mixed
50% / 100% / 150% group by 2% gives 51% / 102% / 153%; a 1% increase is rejected
because some results would be fractional. Decimal changes can be valid:
increasing a 200% object by 0.5% makes it 201%.

text:
Whole scaling changes object sizes and spacing together. Individual scaling
changes object sizes while keeping their positions. Both modes use the same
size restrictions; Clipboard does not silently round or clamp a rejected change.

text:
Both Restore actions set every selected object to exactly 100% size.
Individual Restore keeps all positions. Whole Restore also keeps positions when
the selected sizes differ; if all sizes are equal, it adjusts spacing by the
inverse of that common scale. An already-100% group does not move. Restore is
not an undo history and does not recover earlier mixed-group spacing.

Cost checks look in the current workshop container first. If it covers every
required material, Clipboard can show those local quantities without searching
linked settlements and the player. The read-only cost view offers an optional
full-source total. Otherwise Clipboard checks all sources and labels the totals
accordingly. Viewing costs does not authorize payment.

text:
When payment is enabled, Clipboard asks for confirmation, checks availability
again after the prompt, and verifies withdrawals before placing objects. It
uses the current workshop, then linked workshops, then player inventory. If
payment cannot be completed or verified, placement stops. Resources already
removed are not automatically refunded.

text:
Patterns store object types, positions, rotations, scales, and internal wires.
They also record eligible wire connections to existing objects outside the
selection. Those outside objects are not copied. Reconnecting them requires
the original tool location and valid original endpoints; moving the tool to a
new destination ignores those external connections. Player-created endpoints
are specific to their save. See Clipboard-Object-Filtering.txt for details.

text:
Patterns do not preserve container contents, weapon or armor modifications,
ownership, or script state. SS2 plot plans, levels and settlers are not saved.
If a required plugin or object is unavailable, Clipboard uses a bottlecap
placeholder. Wires attached to missing or filtered placement objects are skipped.

text:
Clipboard reuses an existing object when its base object, position, rotation and
scale match the pattern placement. It avoids creating another copy and can use
the existing object for wire connections. The duplicate-skipped count appears
only when greater than zero, even if import warnings are disabled.

text:
Use Throttling is off by default. It limits placement work and simultaneous
workshop initialization calls. Turning it off may overload scripting and cause
Papyrus stack dumps that interfere with other mods such as Sim Settlements 2.
Completion checks remain active, and turning it off may not shorten the import.
During throttled placement, "Clipboard: Importing objects..." repeats every ten
seconds. Initialization and powering up show progress percentages in either
mode. These report completed work, not elapsed time; wait for the final result.

and power work; successful objects can continue. If Clipboard cannot verify
completion, such as after a timeout or interruption, wiring and power stop for
the whole import.

By default, automatic selection requires an object created during play and
linked to a workshop. Lights also need nonzero object bounds and a workshop
construction recipe. Manual selection is independent of this automatic filter.

text:
The MCM option "Allow Normally Filtered Objects To Be Selected And Exported"
is off by default and broadens automatic selection. Export honors the current
selection, including manually selected objects, regardless of this option.
Permanent exclusions and invalid-object checks still apply. An export with
zero eligible objects does not create or overwrite a pattern.
context: End-user paragraph/section from Clipboard-Object-Filtering.txt, section: SELECTION AND EXPORT. text:
Neither permissive option bypasses Clipboard's infrastructure protections,
configured blacklists, or checks for invalid objects. Settlement workbenches,
Clipboard helpers, objects with the IsMarker flag, and unsupported actor types
remain excluded. Activators (ACTI) and movable statics (MSTT) whose object bounds
are all zero are also always excluded, including from old patterns. This is a
base-object rule, not a hardcoded crop-helper list. The light-source option does
not bypass it. Wire connections are handled separately from object selection.

existing objects outside the selection. Outside endpoints can be plugin-placed
or player-created. They are not added to the copied object list, moved, or
recreated when the pattern is pasted.

and internal wires still import normally. Missing, moved or mismatched original
endpoints are skipped; Clipboard does not search for a nearby replacement.

text:
- "Allow normally filtered light sources to be imported" is off by default.
  Enable it to admit lights without object bounds or a workshop recipe.
- "Disable Havok Physics On Imported Objects" is on by default. It keeps
  imported non-actors from immediately falling or rolling and restores their
  placement if physics moved them during loading. Turn it off for normal loose
  object physics. It does not prevent scripted movement, animation, activation,
  or workshop manipulation, and does not apply this physics change to actors.
- "Use Throttling" is off by default. It limits placement work and simultaneous
  workshop initialization calls. Off may overload scripting and cause Papyrus
  stack dumps that interfere with other mods such as Sim Settlements 2. The
  next import uses the new setting; completion checks remain active in both modes.

text:
Patterns preserve base objects and transforms, not inventories, attached weapon
or armor modifications, or script state. Modified equipment pastes as its
default base object. Missing forms use bottlecap placeholders. Skipping an
object or one of its wires does not shift the other wire connections. Matching
existing objects are reused by base object, position, rotation and scale; new
wires can connect to them without duplicating their placement. Failed or unready
objects are excluded individually when the remaining work is verified complete.
Uncertain completion stops wiring and power for the whole import.

text:
- Uses one package for Fallout 4 OG, NG and AE with matching F4SE and the
  external Runtime Database; includes in-game text for twelve languages.
- Provides a dedicated text and numeric input menu without requiring TIM,
  with keyboard, mouse and controller controls and optional Condition Boy/Girl
  hiding while input is open.
- Accepts rotation and scale input with up to six decimal places. Pattern
  numbers retain the precision of their stored values during export and import.
- Rejects relative scale changes unless every resulting object size is an exact
  whole-number percentage within 1% to 1000%, with guidance on valid changes.
- Makes both Restore actions set every object to 100%. Individual preserves
  positions; Whole adjusts spacing for uniform groups and preserves positions
  for mixed-size groups.
- Checks local workshop materials first, offers full-source totals in cost
  views, and reduces repeated recipe lookups and inventory-query overhead.
  Payment retains confirmation, a fresh availability check and verified removal.
- Honors manually selected objects during export and preserves the existing
  pattern when an export is cancelled, empty or fails validation.
- Records eligible wires to existing objects outside the copied selection,
  reconnecting them only at the source tool position with valid endpoints.
- Improves selection across settlement cells, removes the 128-object truncation
  from large cell/plugin selections and destruction, and reduces repeated
  selection searches and transform calculations.
- Adds separate controls for broader selection/export, light-source import,
  and imported-object physics. Refines SS2 and Auto Beds filters to exclude
  identified generated contents while allowing eligible roots and standalone
  objects; zero-bounds activators and movable statics remain excluded.
- Improves large imports, preserves wire endpoints when objects are skipped,
  reconnects touching conduits, and reuses matching existing placements.
- Waits for required workshop initialization before wiring and power work.
  Verified objects can continue after individual failures; uncertain completion
  stops wiring and power for the whole import. Use Throttling defaults to off.
- Shows periodic placement notices and percentage progress for initialization
  and power. Duplicate-skipped counts appear only when positive.
- Corrects workshop callback arguments, powered-object cleanup, selection-box
  cleanup, pagination and MCM setting routes. Removes temporary profiling tools.
- Always logs warnings, errors and build identities. Optional diagnostic logging
  adds detail; Clipboard.log starts fresh when the game launches.
- Supplies 500 empty pattern slots and preserves support for existing patterns
  and settings. Updates the English user guides under Docs/clipboard.
